title: Repository-Scale Code Intelligence: Cross-File Reasoning, Verified API Migration, and Specification-Driven Test Generation with Coverage Guarantees
background:
Large language models (LLMs) for code have achieved strong performance on function-level synthesis benchmarks such as HumanEval and MBPP, but production software engineering operates at the repository scale, where cross-file dependencies, transitive type constraints, build configurations, and evolving APIs dominate the cost of change. Recent work on retrieval-augmented code models [1] and long-context transformers [2] has expanded the effective reasoning window, yet empirical studies on SWE-bench-style tasks reveal that state-of-the-art agents still resolve fewer than half of real-world issues, with most failures attributable to incomplete context assembly, hallucinated symbols, and fragile multi-step planning [3]. Repository graph encoders [4] and call-graph-aware retrievers have improved localization, but they typically operate on static snapshots and do not reason over version-to-version semantic deltas required for migration tasks.

API migration remains a long-standing pain point: prior systems based on transformation rules or example mining [5] handle syntactic rewrites but break down on semantic shifts (e.g., async refactors, ownership changes, deprecation chains across multiple library versions). Concurrently, automated test generation has progressed from search-based methods (EvoSuite) to neural approaches conditioned on docstrings, yet recent measurement work shows neural tests frequently overfit to implementation, miss specification branches, and provide no formal coverage guarantee [6]. There is no unified framework that (i) grounds LLM reasoning in verifiable repository structure, (ii) certifies behavior-preserving migrations across library versions, and (iii) synthesizes tests from specifications with auditable coverage bounds. Closing this gap is essential for trustworthy AI4Code at the scale of modern software ecosystems.
challenges: Constructing scalable, semantically faithful repository representations that integrate ASTs, def-use chains, type-flow, build graphs, and version histories into a unified context that fits within feasible inference budgets while preserving the precision needed for cross-file symbol resolution

Designing neuro-symbolic agents that decompose multi-file edits into verifiable sub-goals, with grounding mechanisms that prevent symbol hallucination and a planning layer that recovers from partial build/test failures without unbounded retry loops

Formalizing behavior-preserving API migration as a differential equivalence problem across library versions, including semantic diffing of deprecated interfaces, automatic adaptation of call sites with side-effect and concurrency-model changes, and certification via differential testing or bounded model checking

Generating tests directly from natural-language or formal specifications such that coverage (branch, MC/DC, mutation) is provably achieved or its shortfall is explicitly characterized, while avoiding implementation-coupled oracles that defeat regression detection

Establishing repository-scale evaluation protocols and benchmarks that capture longitudinal, multi-commit migration scenarios and specification-anchored test adequacy, going beyond single-issue resolution metrics common in current leaderboards
